clue.text: Work together sealing politician's brief

indicators.note: the outer word closes around the other, sealing it inside

parts.note: to co-act is to act jointly
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A cooperative effort shuts up a politician's short speech or briefing.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact as an adjective means concise or short, which is a sense of brief.

clue.text: Head of CAMRA's description of some ales as rough

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of CAMRA

parts.note: beers brewed with plenty of hops are described as hoppy

explanation.surface: The chief of CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, dismisses some beers as harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppy describes rough water broken into short waves.

clue.text: Picked up tin for one character

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: tin is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: Someone collected a tin as a token for a single figure or letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is strength of character, courage and resolve.

clue.text: Don's swimming in a river among other things

indicators.note: in puts the mixed-up letters within the other pieces

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river

indicators.note: swimming suggests movement, so the letters of the word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A university don takes a dip in a river, among other activities.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a don is a lecturer; the Forth is the Scottish river flowing past Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock way of saying etcetera, indicating further unnamed items.

clue.text: Lead in band downed gins

indicators.note: lead in names the opening letter of the band word
downed means that letter goes down to the bottom, the end, in this down clue

parts.note: a strap is a band of material

explanation.surface: The frontman of a group knocked back several gins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downed gins' suggests drinking; gins here are snares. The S leading STRAP moves to the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a trap for catching animals, from the old word engine.

clue.text: Lacking room, spearmint moved for sage

indicators.note: the remaining letters are moved about into a new order
lacking says the word spearmint goes without those letters

explanation.surface: A herb garden note: without space, the spearmint was shifted to make way for the sage plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sage' looks like the herb beside spearmint, but it is the adjective meaning wise. Removing RM leaves SPEAINT to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a formal word for wise, the adjectival sense of sage.

clue.text: Europeans heated pool upon mounting second filter

indicators.note: upon places the spa on top in this down clue

parts.note: a spa is a hot spring, a heated pool

indicators.note: mounting means going upwards, so the following letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: to drain is to filter out liquid

explanation.surface: Continental tourists warm a pool once they have fitted a second filter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaniards are natives of Spain, which is a European country.

clue.text: Sled carrying this Hollywood star would get spotted

definitions.text: Sled carrying this Hollywood star would get spotted

parts.words: Sled carrying this Hollywood star would get spotted
parts.note: the star's surname placed inside the word sled spells a word meaning spotted, flecked with marks

explanation.surface: A movie star riding a sledge would be recognised by fans.
explanation.walkthrough: S-PECK-LED is speckled, meaning spotted; the star is Gregory Peck, of To Kill a Mockingbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregory Peck was a leading Hollywood actor of the 1940s to 1960s.

clue.text: Occasional large-scale arrests as detective

indicators.note: arrests means the outer word holds the others inside it

parts.note: an epic is grand and large-scale
so can mean as, in the sense of thus
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A police headline: occasional big round-ups as an inspector cracks down.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic means happening at irregular intervals, sporadic rather than continuous.

clue.text: Time was important, scrubbing top being worn

indicators.note: scrubbing top removes the first letter, the top in this down clue

parts.note: mattered means was important

explanation.surface: Punctuality mattered, so someone scrubbed the worn surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattered clothing is ragged and threadbare, worn out through long use.

clue.text: Exposed stripped body seen around Aussie's truck

indicators.note: the trimmed body is placed around the truck, enclosing it
stripped means the word body loses its outer letters

parts.note: a ute is the Australian term for a utility truck or pickup

explanation.surface: A naked corpse found near an Australian pickup sounds like a crime report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripped' looks like nakedness but means the word loses its outer letters; 'ute' is Australian slang for a pickup.
explanation.definitionFit: To out someone is to expose them publicly, so outed is a synonym of exposed.

clue.text: This subversive welcoming Timon would be against royalty

parts.words: This subversive welcoming Timon would be against royalty
parts.note: TIMON placed between the answer's AN and ARCHIST makes a word meaning opposed to monarchy

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's misanthrope Timon is admitted by a rebel who would oppose the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Put TIMON inside AN-ARCHIST and it becomes ANTIMONARCHIST, someone against royalty; the clue describes the subversive by what it would become.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist rejects all government and is a classic example of a subversive figure.

clue.text: Edge back deep with player on field and cover for prop

indicators.note: back says the word for edge is read backwards

parts.note: a lip is an edge or rim
a deep voice or note is low
slip is a cricket fielding position, so a fielder there

explanation.surface: Rugby talk: a back plays deep with another player on the field, covering for the prop forward.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a prop is a front-row forward, which the surface plays on; here a prop is something to lean on, a pillow. Slip is a cricket fielder close behind the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillowslip is the cloth case that covers a pillow, and a pillow props up the head.

clue.text: Tolerated swine in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a boar is a male pig, a swine

explanation.surface: Someone put up with a pig of a person while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore is the past tense of bear, which means to put up with or endure.

clue.text: Produced ranges including English cakes

parts.note: made means produced

indicators.note: including puts the letter inside the ranges word

parts.note: lines can mean ranges or rows

explanation.surface: A baker turns out cookers with English cakes among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeleines are small French sponge cakes baked in shell-shaped moulds, made famous by Proust.

clue.text: Blue container inside oven's loaded with rice

indicators.note: inside puts the container within the rearranged letters
loaded suggests a drunken or jumbled state, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a vat is a large container for liquids

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: a blue dish placed in an oven packed with rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like the colour of the container, but it is the political sense: blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, so a blue is a Tory supporter.

clue.text: Extra money cleaner received in rise

indicators.note: received in means the cleaner sits inside the rise word

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rise
a char is a cleaning woman, British for a charlady

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady got extra cash as part of a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional fee added on top of the usual price.

clue.text: Elusive craft stall's first playpen assembled

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of stall
assembled means put together from parts, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A market trader puts together the stall's first playpen, a craft of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' hints at aircraft stalling, but here it only supplies S.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy plane is an aircraft designed to gather reconnaissance while evading detection.

clue.text: Supplied dough for month, bread provided in return

indicators.note: in return means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: DEC is the abbreviation for December
nan is an Indian flatbread
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Someone gave baking dough monthly, getting bread back in exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' looks like baking but is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is slang for money, so supplying it for something is paying for it.

clue.text: Drag empty tub by grasses, ones bearing bristles

parts.note: a drag is a tedious nuisance, a pain

indicators.note: empty means the word tub has its contents, the inner letter, removed

parts.note: emptied of its middle letter, tub leaves its outer letters
rushes are grass-like marsh plants

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a bathtub past the reeds where bristly creatures live.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintbrushes are tools with tufts of bristles on a handle for applying colour.

clue.text: Deliverer leaving starter from Indian — enjoy!

indicators.note: leaving means that letter goes out of the deliverer word

parts.note: a saviour delivers people from danger

indicators.note: starter from takes the first letter of Indian

explanation.surface: A takeaway driver drops off a starter from the Indian restaurant: bon appétit!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliverer' and 'starter' suggest a takeaway; the deliverer is a saviour and the starter is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: To savour food is to enjoy and relish its taste slowly.

clue.text: Church aisle not a winding shape

indicators.note: winding means twisting around, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not says the word aisle goes without its a

explanation.surface: A church aisle that runs straight rather than curving.
explanation.walkthrough: AISLE without A leaves ISLE, which is rearranged to ISEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To chisel is to cut and shape wood or stone with a bladed tool.

clue.text: Climber last in trek reaching summit

parts.note: the pea is a climbing plant

indicators.note: last in picks the final letter of trek

explanation.surface: A mountaineer at the end of a trek arrives at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' looks like a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is the pointed top of a mountain, which is what a summit is.

clue.text: Rise with good beer knocked back in quiet club

indicators.note: in places the rise and reversed beer within the call for quiet

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a hill is a rise in the ground

indicators.note: knocked back means the good beer is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker rises with a decent pint downed quietly in a social club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking, but it reverses G and ALE to ELAG. 'Club' is a weapon, not a social club.
explanation.definitionFit: A shillelagh is an Irish cudgel, a thick wooden stick used as a weapon.

clue.text: Taxed home in California?

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, standing for California here
a den is a home or lair

explanation.surface: Is a house in California subject to heavy tax?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxed' suggests property tax; it means burdened.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily loaded or burdened, as is someone taxed by a heavy demand.

clue.text: Love booze-up occasionally being served up this, perhaps

definitions.text: Love booze-up occasionally being served up this, perhaps

parts.note: love is zero, O, in tennis scoring

indicators.note: served up means those letters are read upwards in this down clue
occasionally takes every other letter of booze-up

explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of booze-up give OZU, served up as UZO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouzo is an aniseed-flavoured Greek spirit, the sort of drink poured at a booze-up.

clue.text: Bill shunning new colour gets dressed

indicators.note: shunning means the bill word does without that letter

parts.note: an account is a bill to be settled
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill avoids a new hue and puts on clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an invoice, ACCOUNT, which loses N to give ACCOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Accoutred means equipped or attired, especially in special clothing or gear.

clue.text: Presumably, disapprovals displayed for retreats

definitions.meaning: second meaning: secluded corners, places to retreat to

explanation.walkthrough: 'Presumably' warns of a playful reading: split the answer as NO OKs and it is a set of refusals.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small sheltered corner, the kind of hideaway or retreat one withdraws to.

clue.text: Explanation of text friend, not enemy, bored by

indicators.note: the answer lies inside these words, as if bored into them

explanation.surface: Someone is bored by a message from a friend rather than a foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Text' looks like a phone message to a friend, but the answer runs through 'friEND NOT Enemy'.
explanation.definitionFit: An endnote is a note at the end of a book or chapter explaining or citing part of the text.

clue.text: Criminal sort in jail's last bit of snout

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are rearranged
last picks the final letter of jail

parts.note: the word jail, whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A villainous type locked up as a snout, prison slang for an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a snout is a police informer and also tobacco in prison; here it is simply a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is one of the two openings in a nose or snout.
